q: 1. In a venturiflume, the flow takes place at ............
explain: Since a venturiflume is an open channel structure, the water surface is in contact with the atmosphere, so flow occurs at atmospheric pressure.

q: 2. A venturiflume is used to measure ............
options: pressure difference between two points in a channel
pressure difference between two points in a pipe
explain: A venturiflume is the open-channel equivalent of a venturi meter, used specifically to measure the discharge ($Q$).

q: 3. The coefficient of venturiflume, generally, lies between ............
explain: Venturiflumes are very efficient with minimal energy loss, so their coefficient of discharge ($C_d$) is typically between 0.95 and 1.0.

q: 4. In a venturimeter, the divergent cone is kept ...............
explain: The divergent cone is made longer with a smaller angle (5°-7°) to prevent flow separation and minimize energy loss due to eddy formation.

q: 5. The instrument used for measuring the velocity of flow is known as ...............
explain: While venturi and orifice meters measure discharge (Q), the pitot tube is specifically designed to measure point velocity (v).

q: 6. An orifice is an opening in a vessel with ...............
options: closed perimeter of regular shape through which water flows
the water level of the liquid on the upstream side below the top of the orifice
prolonged sides having length of 2 to 3 diameters of the opening in thick wall.
explain: An orifice is defined as a closed-perimeter opening through which fluid flows for measurement or discharge purposes.

q: 7. Hydraulic coefficient of an orifice means the coefficient of ...............
explain: Hydraulic coefficients include Cv (velocity), Cc (contraction), and Cd (discharge), along with Cr (resistance).

q: 8. In a short cylindrical external mouthpiece, the venacontracta occurs at a distance from the outlet of orifice equal to ...............
options: one-fourth the diameter of the orifice
one-third the diameter of the orifice
tow-third the diameter of the orifice
explain: In an external mouthpiece, the vena contracta typically forms at a distance of about 0.5 to 0.67 times the diameter from the entrance.

q: 9. The shape of fire hose nozzle is generally kept ...............
explain: Convergent nozzles are used to increase the velocity of the liquid jet for fire fighting purposes.

q: 10. Short tube mouthpiece will not run full at its outlet if the head under which the orifice works, is ...............
options: less than 12.2 m of the water
more than 12.2 m of the water
equal of 12.2 m of the water
explain: If the head exceeds a certain limit (~12m), the negative pressure at the vena contracta becomes too high, causing the jet to separate and not run full.

q: 11. In an inclined position, a venturimeter records ...............
explain: A venturimeter is independent of orientation (horizontal, vertical, or inclined) because it measures the differential head (h), which remains constant for the same flow.

q: 12. If H is the difference of liquid levels on two sides of an orifice (width b, depth d), the discharge through the orifice will be ...............
explain: The standard discharge formula for a small orifice is Q = Cd * Area * √(2gH), where Area = b * d.

q: 13. An orifice is called a large orifice if water head, is ...............
options: twice the diameter of the orifice
thrice the diameter of the orifice
four times the diameter of the orifice
five times the diameter of the orifice
explain: An orifice is considered 'large' if the head of water is less than 5 times the depth or diameter of the orifice, as the velocity variation across the opening becomes significant.

q: 14. Discharge through a totally submerged orifice, is directly proportional to ...............
options: difference in elevation of water surfaces
square root of the difference in elevation of water surface
reciprocal of the area of the opening
explain: For a submerged orifice, the discharge $Q$ is given by $Q = C_d \cdot A \sqrt{2g(H_1 - H_2)}$, where $(H_1 - H_2)$ is the difference in liquid levels.

q: 15. The width of a weir with end contraction, is ...............
options: equal to the width of the channel
less than the width of the channel
half the width of the channel
explain: A weir with end contractions has a crest length shorter than the channel width, causing the water stream to contract horizontally.

q: 16. The upper surface of the weir over which water flows, is known as ...............
explain: The 'sill' or 'crest' is the top edge of the weir over which water flows. The 'nappe' refers to the actual sheet of water flowing over it.

q: 17. If S is the length of the crest, H is the height of water source of a weir whose length is L and discharge is Q m³/sec, the velocity of approach Va is ...............
explain: The velocity of approach is the flow velocity in the channel leading to the weir, calculated as Discharge (Q) divided by the Flow Area (Length L × Total Depth [Head H + Crest Height S]).

q: 18. When water flows over a rectangular suppressed weir, the negative pressure created beneath the nappe ...............
explain: Negative pressure (vacuum) under the nappe sucks the water sheet downwards, increasing the effective head and thereby increasing the discharge.

q: 19. When no air is left below the nappe and water stream adheres to the downstream face of the weir, it is known as ...............
explain: A clinging nappe occurs when the air is exhausted from the space beneath the nappe, causing it to 'cling' to the weir's downstream face.

q: 20. With a clinging nappe of a weir, the excess discharge, is ...............
explain: Because of the lack of ventilation and the resulting vacuum effect, the discharge for a clinging nappe can be significantly higher (up to 25-30%) than a free nappe.

q: 21. The notch angle for maximum discharge over a triangular notch, is ...............
explain: A 90° V-notch (triangular notch) is standard for maximum efficiency and ease of calculation in water measurement.

q: 22. The discharge through a V-notch weir varies as ...............
explain: The discharge formula for a triangular notch is $Q =  rac{8}{15} C_d 	an(	heta/2) \sqrt{2g} H^{5/2}$.

q: 23. A stepped notch is a combination of ...............
explain: A stepped notch consists of multiple rectangular sections of varying widths, used to measure discharge that varies widely over time.

q: 24. The ratio of the percentage error in the discharge and percentage error in the measurement of head, over rectangular notch, is ...............
explain: Since $Q \propto H^{3/2}$ for a rectangular notch, $ rac{dQ}{Q} =  rac{3}{2}  rac{dH}{H}$.

q: 25. The ratio of the percentage error in the discharge and percentage error in the measurement of head over a triangular notch, is ...............
explain: Since $Q \propto H^{5/2}$ for a triangular notch, $ rac{dQ}{Q} =  rac{5}{2}  rac{dH}{H}$.

q: 26. If H is height of the liquid above the sill, the effect of end contractions, according to Francis formula, is ...............
explain: Francis formula states that each end contraction reduces the effective length of the weir by $0.1H$.

q: 27. Cippoletti weir is a ...............
options: rectangular weir hose length is kept 3 times the height of the water above sill
triangular weir whose notch angle is 90°
trapezoidal weir, whose sides slope 1 horizontal to 4 verticals
a combination of rectangular and triangular weirs
explain: A Cippoletti weir is a trapezoidal weir with side slopes of 1:4 (horizontal to vertical). This specific slope is designed to compensate for the reduction in discharge due to end contractions.

q: 28. The thickness of a sharp crested weir is kept less than ...............
options: one-third of the height of water on the sill
one-half of the height of water on the sill
two-third of the height of water on the sill
explain: To ensure that the water spring (nappe) touches only the upstream edge and stays clear of the crest, the thickness of a sharp-crested weir should be less than half the head of water ($H/2$).

q: 29. Discharge over an ogee weir remains the same as that of ...............
explain: An ogee weir is designed to follow the lower profile of a nappe from a sharp-crested weir; therefore, its discharge characteristics are ideally the same as those of a sharp-crested weir.

q: 30. Flow of water in pipes of diameter more than 3 meter can be measured by ...............
explain: For very large diameter pipes where installing a venturimeter is impractical/expensive, a Pitot tube is used to measure velocity at various points to determine discharge.

q: 31. An orifice is taken as large if ...............
explain: In practice, if the depth of the orifice ($d = H_2 - H_1$) is greater than about one-third of the head ($H$), it is treated as a large orifice.

q: 32. The discharge formula Q = Cd √(2gH) × A is used to rectangular ...............
explain: This standard formula assumes the velocity is constant across the area, which is only valid for 'small' orifices where the head is large compared to the orifice depth.

q: 33. The discharge through an internal mouth piece is more if its length is ...............
explain: When the length is at least 3 times the diameter (running full), the mouthpiece acts like a short pipe, increasing the coefficient of discharge ($C_d$) to about 0.707.

q: 34. the inlet length of a venturimeter ...............
options: is equal to the outlet length
is more than the outlet length
is less than the outlet length
explain: The diverging (outlet) section of a venturimeter is made longer than the converging (inlet) section to prevent flow separation and minimize energy loss.

q: 35. Pitot-tube is used for measurement of
explain: A Pitot tube measures the stagnation pressure to determine the local velocity of the fluid at the specific point where the tube is placed.

q: 36. Pitot-tube is used to measure
explain: A Pitot tube is a primary instrument used to measure the local or point velocity of flow by converting kinetic energy into pressure energy at the stagnation point.

q: 37. Venturimeter is used to measure
explain: A venturimeter is a device based on Bernoulli's principle used specifically for measuring the rate of flow (discharge) through a pipeline.

q: 38. Orifice-meter is used to measure
explain: Similar to a venturimeter, an orifice-meter is a cheaper alternative used to measure the discharge or rate of flow in a pipe by creating a pressure drop.

q: 39. The rate of flow through a venturimeter varies as
explain: The discharge formula for a venturimeter is Q = [Cd × A1 × A2 × √(2gh)] / √(A1² - A2²). Thus, Q is proportional to the square root of the head (√H).

q: 40. The rate of flow through a V-notch varies as
explain: For a triangular notch (V-notch), the discharge Q is proportional to H^(5/2), where H is the head over the notch.

q: 41. The range for co-efficient of discharge (Cd) for a venturimeter is
explain: Venturimeters are highly efficient with streamlined flow, leading to a very high coefficient of discharge, typically between 0.95 and 0.99.

q: 42. An orifice is known as large orifice when the head of liquid from the centre of orifice is
options: more than 10 times the depth of orifice
less than 10 times the depth of orifice
less than 5 times the depth of orifice
explain: If the head of liquid (H) is less than 5 to 10 times the depth of the orifice (d), the velocity varies significantly across the orifice, classifying it as a large orifice.

q: 43. Which mouthpiece is having maximum co-efficient of discharge?
explain: A convergent-divergent mouthpiece minimizes energy loss and prevents flow separation, resulting in a coefficient of discharge that can reach 1.0.

q: 44. The co-efficient of discharge (Cd)
options: for an orifice is more than that for a mouthpiece
for internal mouthpiece is more than that external
for a mouthpiece is more than that for an orifice
explain: Mouthpieces generally have a higher Cd (around 0.82 for external) compared to a sharp-edged orifice (around 0.62) because they reduce the contraction of the jet.

q: 45. Orifices are used to measure
explain: An orifice is an opening in a vessel used primarily to control or measure the rate of flow (discharge) of a fluid.

q: 46. Mouthpieces are used to measure
explain: A mouthpiece is a short tube attached to an orifice, also used for measuring the rate of flow or discharge from a tank.

q: 47. The ratio of actual discharge of a jet of water to its theoretical discharge is known as
explain: The Coefficient of Discharge (Cd) is defined as the ratio of Actual Discharge (Qact) to Theoretical Discharge (Qth).

q: 48. The ratio of the area of the jet of water at veena-contracta to the area of orifice is known as
explain: The Coefficient of Contraction (Cc) is the ratio of the area of the jet at the vena contracta to the area of the orifice.

q: 49. Notch is a device used for measuring
options: rate of flow through a small channel
explain: Notches are used to measure the discharge in open channels or small streams, whereas meters like the venturimeter are used for closed pipes.

q: 50. The velocity with which the water approaches a notch is called
explain: Velocity of approach is the average velocity of the liquid in the channel just upstream of the notch or weir.
